source.repro: pnpm --filter @jbrowse/web build, then in products/jbrowse-web: node browser-tests/probe-uniform-ring.ts [--dpr=2] [--tracks=a,b]
source.notes: Headless Chrome with --use-gl=angle on a MacBook Pro (AMD RDNA-1 under WebGPU), 1600x900 viewport, a 1588 px LinearGenomeView on volvox ctgA:1-6000. Every GPUDevice.createBuffer, createTexture and GPUQueue.writeBuffer in the page is wrapped. A ring is a UNIFORM buffer sized MAX_UNIFORM_SLOTS x its aligned slot, allocated once per display as a GPU buffer AND a Uint8Array staging copy, so the CPU column is the GPU column. `msaa` is the 4x colour attachment each display allocates, at w x h x 4 bytes x 4 samples — the swap-chain texture is not counted, since it comes from getCurrentTexture rather than createTexture. `data` is every other GPU buffer, which is the instance data the tracks actually drew. `peak slots` is the largest slot count any one display's ring reached in a frame, from the single writeBuffer endFrame issues per frame (bytes / aligned slot size); it did not move between load and 30 frames of panning. The dpr 1 arm is volvox_alignments + volvox_cram_alignments; the dpr 2 arm adds volvox_alignments_grouped_by_strand (two groups, the row that reaches 4 slots), volvox-long-reads-sv-bam, volvox_sv and volvox_bam_pileup.
